content.text:
62:## Option 2: `openclaw mcp add`
63-
64-OpenClaw keeps MCP servers under `mcp.servers` in `~/.openclaw/openclaw.json`
65-(`openclaw config schema` shows the key path). Register gbrain with the CLI,
66-then run `gbrain setup openclaw` so a new session knows to use it:
67-
68-```bash
69-openclaw mcp add gbrain --command "$(command -v gbrain)" --arg serve --arg --surface --arg starter --arg --advertise --arg verbs --env GBRAIN_HOME=$HOME
70-gbrain setup openclaw
71-```
72-
73-The second line is not optional. Without it the tools are registered but
74-nothing tells the agent to use them, and a new session answers from OpenClaw's
75-own memory and chat history instead (in the [install eval](https://github.com/garrytan/harness-evals/blob/master/docs/benchmarks/2026-11-17-gbrain-install/results/README.md),
76-11 of the 30 OpenClaw runs without gbrain's install block missed this way).
77-See [Brain-first instructions](#brain-first-instructions).
78-
79-Use an absolute `--command` path: the launchd-started gateway's `PATH` does
80-not include `~/.bun/bin`, so a bare `gbrain` fails to spawn. `--env` is
81-optional: a PGLite brain needs no `DATABASE_URL`
82-(`--env DATABASE_URL=postgresql://...` for Postgres), and `GBRAIN_HOME` only
83-matters when the brain home isn't `~/.gbrain`. `--surface starter --advertise verbs`
84-lists the seven-verb memory protocol ([MEMORY_VERBS v1](../protocol/MEMORY_VERBS_v1.md))
85-plus `request_tools`, which reaches every other tool; drop the
86-`--advertise verbs` values to list the starter set (`full` for the whole catalog) (check
87-`openclaw mcp add --help` for your version's `--arg` spelling).
88-
89-Leave `GBRAIN_SOURCE` unset in the MCP env unless you deliberately want
90-single-source retrieval: a pin scopes every tool (search, `get_brain_identity`
91-counts, …) to that one source, and nothing warns on reads.
92-
93-## Remote brain: OpenClaw's MCP client over HTTPS

Usage: gbrain forget <fact-id> [--reason <text>] [--source <id>] [--request-id <uuid>] [--json]
       (withdraws the fact: it expires and cannot be re-saved; the text stays in history and backups)
       gbrain forget <fact-id> --purge [--dry-run] [--yes --request-id <uuid>] [--reason <text>] [--all-subjects] [--vacuum] [--reason-scan-limit <n>] [--source <id>] [--json]
       gbrain forget --purge --match "<text>"
       gbrain forget --purge --status --request-id <uuid> [--continue]

Purge family (remove content from live stores; never physical erasure):
  gbrain forget <id> --purge            purge one fact's claim (dry-run receipt, then a typed token)
  gbrain delete <slug> --purge          purge a page and its derived rows, with a page tombstone
  gbrain pages purge-deleted            hard-delete pages soft-deleted more than 72h ago
  gbrain sources purge <id>             remove a whole source
  gbrain pages purges list              list page purge tombstones
  gbrain pages unpurge <slug>           clear a page tombstone so the content can be imported again

content.text:
gbrain is set up and connected to OpenClaw, using the defaults and no API keys. It takes effect when you start a new session, because OpenClaw reads its instruction file at session start.

**What I set up:**
- **Brain:** a local brain (stored on this machine, created with `gbrain init --pglite --no-embedding`). Nothing leaves the machine. Settings I left at their defaults:
  - Search mode is conservative.
  - Agents only save what you explicitly ask them to remember.
  - Free background upkeep is on.
  - A redacted conversation archive is on.
- **OpenClaw connection:** gbrain is registered as an MCP server named `gbrain`, using the absolute path to the program. I started it once by hand and it listed its 8 tools: remember, recall, entity, synthesize, forget, context_pack, delta and request_tools.
- **Brain-first setup:** `gbrain setup openclaw` created `/workspace/AGENTS.md` with a "check GBrain first" section. It also installed a small plugin, `gbrain-turn-rule`, that repeats that rule on every message. The first run said the plugin wasn't loaded, but it showed as loaded on the next check, and a re-run of the setup then passed.
- **Test:** saving a test fact and recalling it worked. I then withdrew the test fact.

**Things to know:**
- **Search is keyword-only.** Without an embedding API key, search matches words only, and near-duplicate facts aren't caught. This is the expected trade-off for staying free.
- **Two `gbrain doctor` warnings:**
  - `brain_score` is expected because the brain is still empty.
  - `provenance_stamp_drift` is probably from my test fact. Its fix is marked "ask user", so I didn't run it. If you want it fixed: `gbrain repair provenance --source default`.
- **Updates may suggest leaving your version.** gbrain's self-update is set to notify you about the stable channel, not install automatically. Your pinned v0.60.760.0 stays unless you choose to switch, but it may suggest moving to `stable`.
- **I couldn't confirm the live gateway picked up the changes.** The OpenClaw config tool errored when I asked it to reload, and the plugins tool said there was no running gateway. If gbrain doesn't show up in a new session, restart the gateway.
- **Optional:** if you want agents to save facts you state without being asked, run `gbrain config set memory.auto_writeback salient`. gbrain recommends this for a personal brain.
